Class RegionConstants

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.RegionConstants
public final class RegionConstants extends Object
Single source of truth for the region-positioning layout constants — stacking gaps and edge insets — shared across all four region contexts (MenuRegion, SlotGroupRegion, HudRegion, ScreenRegion) and both pure math helpers (RegionMath, SlotGroupRegionMath).

Why a shared home (Phase 3b — Item 4c centralize)

These constants previously lived inconsistently: RegionMath held STACK_GAP = 2 (consumed by the menu, slot-group, AND HUD prefix paths), ScreenRegion held its own STACK_GAP = 4 + EDGE_INSET = 4, and HudRegion held EDGE_INSET = 4 but no stack gap of its own (the HUD prefix path borrowed RegionMath.STACK_GAP). Four declarations, three of which had to stay in lock-step by hand. This class hoists them into one place so a value lives in exactly one spot.

This is the single public home (Phase 5 — symmetry pass). The per-enum constant faces (ScreenRegion.STACK_GAP/ EDGE_INSET, HudRegion.EDGE_INSET) were removed so all four region enums present an identical surface — consumers read the values here. (The lone exception is HudRegion.CENTER_CROSSHAIR_CLEARANCE, a genuinely HUD-only value with no equivalent in the other three contexts, which stays on HudRegion.) Values are unchanged — no visual change.

Per-context values are PRESERVED, not collapsed

Centralizing must not move a single pixel — the gap values Trev has seen in-game stay exactly as they were. So the two distinct gaps are kept as two NAMED constants rather than unified:
  • MENU_STACK_GAP (= 2) — the menu / slot-group / HUD stacking gap. These three contexts all stacked at a 2px gap before the hoist (the menu + slot-group math used RegionMath.STACK_GAP; the HUD prefix path likewise used RegionMath.STACK_GAP), so they all point here.
  • SCREEN_STACK_GAP (= 4) — the vanilla non-container screen stacking gap. Only the vanilla-screen prefix path used the wider 4px gap before the hoist, so it alone points here.

The two values are deliberately NOT collapsed into one — doing so would shift either the menu/slot-group/HUD layouts (to 4) or the vanilla-screen layout (to 2), a visual change Trev hasn't approved.

Edge inset

EDGE_INSET (= 4) is the screen-edge inset shared by the HUD and vanilla-screen contexts (both previously declared their own identical EDGE_INSET = 4, matching vanilla's F3 debug-overlay convention). The menu + slot-group contexts anchor to a frame rather than a screen edge, so they have no edge inset.

    • SCREEN_EDGE_MARGIN

      public static final int SCREEN_EDGE_MARGIN
      Screen-edge safe-area margin (pixels, GUI-scaled) for the adaptive layout foundation (Pass 3). Every panel keeps at least this margin from each physical screen edge; when a panel's natural content would cross it, the panel wraps/reflows instead of overflowing (Panel.setAvailableContentWidth(int)).

      = 6 — a touch more breathing room than EDGE_INSET (which is the HUD/vanilla-screen anchor inset) so an adaptive panel doesn't sit flush against the window edge. The two are intentionally distinct: EDGE_INSET positions edge-anchored panels; SCREEN_EDGE_MARGIN is the hard "do not cross" boundary every panel's width budget is measured against.
